newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak PM to re-impose car import duty Jan 1-paper.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM to re-impose car import duty Jan 1-paper.

text.p: Slovakia will re-impose a 7.5 percent duty on imports of new cars with engines of 1,500cc from January 1 next year, Narodna Obroda, the country's leading economic newspaper, reported on Friday.

"From the beginning of 1997, Slovakia will impose the same customs duties on imported cars, as were in place before the temporary abolition last year," the daily quoted Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar as saying.

In September 1995, Slovakia temporarily abolished customs duties on imported medium-sized cars, saying it would review the policy at the end of 1996, taking into account the state of the foreign trade balance.
The abolition of the duties was an attempt to help Slovaks trying to buy medium-sized cars and help eliminate the number of older cars from the road.
But the trade deficit has since ballooned, spurred in large part by imports of new cars.
Slovakia posted a trade deficit of 31.9 billion crowns in January-July, reversing the 1.8 billion crown surplus in 1995.

Earlier this year the government decided to abolish a widely criticised import surcharge effective January 1, 1997 after heavy pressure from western economic organisations such as the WTO, and from the European Union.
